claim: Simple turns are FAST and the fast path never bypasses safety. The measured bottleneck (reports/performance_baseline.md, instrumented not guessed): a trivial greeting routed through the 8B local model = ~14s, while a known fact (deterministic) is 0.1s. anima/route_classifier.py classifies greetings/acks/presence-checks/how-are-you as simple_chat and answers them with a fast, in-character DETERMINISTIC reply wired BEFORE the model call in mouth.respond — so a simple turn does NO 8B inference (measured 0.02-0.16s vs 14s) while the SAME safety gates still run on the text (final_output_gate + the #1-rule backstop + completeness). 'how are you?' is also SAFER on the fast path: a deterministic redirect cannot confabulate inner life (the exact #1-rule failure the 8B model risks). Real questions fall through to the model unchanged. HARD-gated: classifier correctness, fast-reply safety (passes the gate, non-hostile, no #1-rule break), the fast path wired before the model, and live simple/known turns under the < 5s hard budget. The 8B model latency on normal chat is reported HONESTLY (warn), not faked green — it is the next optimization (model policy / smaller model / capped tokens).
owner: anima/route_classifier.py (classify/is_simple_chat/simple_reply), anima/mouth.py (fast path wired before the selected per-turn brain.reply), scripts/certify_response_latency.py, scripts/benchmark_turns.py, reports/performance_baseline.md

The normal 8B model turn is reported honestly (warn), never faked.

known_gaps: This phase hard-gates the SIMPLE/known routes (the 'feels broken' moments) and the fast-path safety. The 8B local model on NORMAL chat (real questions / source answers) is still ~9-14s — reported honestly as a WARN, not hidden. The next performance lane (directive §11 model policy + §8 retrieval budgets + §10 immune tiering) reduces that: pressure-aware keep_alive, a smaller/faster model or capped tokens for normal chat, and capped source context. The full perf_trace stage breakdown + Founder Console performance panel are also next.
